principalConclusion: ARA must model research and analytics through explicit, versioned layers: question/purpose → protocol → condition → authorized observable event or instrument → measure → construct → interpretation → decision/action. No layer may be inferred automatically from the previous one. Personal analytics, teaching support, research analytics and operational observability require separate authority, visibility, retention and permitted-use policies.
recommendedPath: Keep the AraLearn minimal functional-state profile as the default personal baseline.
Represent protocols and conditions as versioned objects that lock content, configuration, instruments, assignment and provenance when comparison requires it.
Authorize events selectively by purpose; do not collect every technically possible event.
Separate event vocabulary, measures, constructs, interpretations and interventions.
Require formula, unit, window, missing-data handling, limitation and permitted use for every measure.
Use named role-oriented analytics questions rather than a universal technical dashboard.
Keep personal analytics opt-in and separate from institutional or research visibility.
Treat consent, withdrawal, minimisation, retention, access and export as protocol parameters with rights-based precedence.
Support external vocabularies such as Caliper/xAPI through mappings, not as the ARA domain model.
Require variant diffs and immutable provenance snapshots for comparative courses and microsequence compositions.
Separate operational telemetry from educational/research analytics.
Defer production event schemas, databases, dashboards, metric formulas and participant studies to #5/#6/#7/#8.

deferredCandidates.reason: Conceptual vocabulary and authorized layers must precede storage and transport design.
Measures depend on concrete research questions, instruments and validity evidence.
Requires valid constructs, fairness analysis, human review and proportional interventions.
Causal claims depend on design and assumptions, not a platform feature.
Views must be role- and question-oriented.
Exposure and completion are not mastery; evidence and equivalence are unresolved.
No participant study is authorized by P4.

rejectedOrNotRecommended: Collect all possible events by default.
Treat clicks, time, delay, retries, interruption or navigation as direct measures of attention, effort, engagement, difficulty or mastery.
Use one analytics dashboard for all roles.
Expose individual data to teachers, institutions or researchers merely because it exists.
Use pseudonymisation as if it were anonymisation.
Retain identifiable data indefinitely for future unspecified use.
Treat Caliper, xAPI or any external standard as the complete ARA analytics model.
Combine operational logs with educational analytics without explicit purpose and authorization.
Use opaque prediction for punitive or high-consequence decisions.
Call a comparison randomized, causal, pre-registered or reproducible without the required method and record.
